_doc: #624 — this app's RUNTIME ARTIFACT declared as a fleet lib, so the 370 MB Nix bootstrap #618 moved out of the APK is a named, versioned member of the constellation instead of an anonymous release asset. Nothing about the artifact is restated here: `declared_in` + `at` POINT at the one #618 declaration (build.json::forks.nixdroid.bootstrap.artifact), and data/regen.sh resolves the identity, the asset names and the urls from there. This file exists only to say WHO the artifact is to the fleet — the module name every other identity is derived from, per #474's one-declaration rule.
_doc_not_in_build_json: Deliberately its own file and NOT a key in build.json, which is load-bearing here: build.json is the first of this artifact's identity_files, so a fleet key added to it would change the content address, rename the asset, republish 370 MB and make every phone refetch it — for a change that alters no byte of the bootstrap. The sibling ac_cloud-termux keeps the same shape so the two are read by one scan.
_doc_module: The ONE name. id = lib-{module}, label = cloud-lib-{module} (#474, the same rule regen.sh applies to every lib APK). Not written out twice.
_doc_kind: NOT `app` and NOT `lib`: there is no APK and no package id here, so this entry is emitted into constellation-fleet.json's `catalogue`, never its `apps`. Fleet.parse reads only `apps`, so the updater, both auto-update workers and every install path are structurally incapable of being handed this row — a 370 MB installable APK is not merely discouraged, it cannot be constructed. The Constellation page draws catalogue rows from the same declared group as everything else.
what: The proot + Nix store bootstrap this terminal logs into, with the agent tool belt already realized as a Nix profile generation. Fetched once from the release beside the APK, sha256-gated against the digest baked into assets/, extracted on first launch and never refetched while the digest matches.
